text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele announces his resignation and says that the political elite and President Guntis Ulmanis have unambiguosly questioned the moral principles behind the cabinet formation. Shkele said he cannot keep working without the support of the president and parliament.

- Most ruling political factions say the prime minister's resignation came as a total surprise and exclude the possibility for Andris Shkele to be re-nominated by the president as the next cabinet-maker.
- Ulmanis said he never denied support to Shkele. He called allegations by Andris Shkele that he failed to get in touch with him "a pure lie", saying he has been in his office all the time.

- Several potential candidates to form the new cabinet have been named behind the scenes: Anatoly Gorbunovs, Andris Berzins, Vilis Krishtopans (all representatives of the Latvia's Way), Ventspils mayor Aivars Lembergs and Ziedonis Chevers of the Democratic Party Saimnieks. Some politicans mention Shkele might be re-entrusted to make the cabinet once again.

- Newly-appointed Minister Finance Vassily Melnik said he is ready to resign to keep Shkele and the government. Ulmanis, in turn, said his opinion about Melnik as an unsuitable candidate for the post of finance minister has not changed.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton is likely to meet his Baltic counterparts in Sweden while visiting Europe in early July.
- The board of the party Latvia's Way has approved the list of its candidates for Riga and seven other major cities.

- BNS news agency reports that the mayor of the eastern town of Daugavpils, Alexei Vidavski, has joined the list of candidates of the Democratic Party Saimnieks in Daugavpils. Vadaski has been banned from standing as he is not a Latvian citizen.
- A Russian version of memoirs by President Ulmanis will be presented to the public on January 22.

- President Ulmanis paid tribute to the victims of January 1991 and laid flowers at the Freedom Monument . There have also been also commemoration ceremonies in the Ministry of Interior and cemeteries.
